steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Audience reception of global film is shaped by cultural context: viewers from different backgrounds interpret the same film differently based on their own values and experiences.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Subtitles preserve the original language performance and cultural authenticity but require active reading and can distract from visual composition.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dubbing allows viewers to focus entirely on the image but replaces original vocal performances and can flatten cultural specificity through translation choices.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cultural bridging occurs when a film from one culture resonates with audiences from another, often through universal themes such as family, love or justice.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always consider how your own cultural position as a UK viewer affects your interpretation of a global film. When discussing subtitles versus dubbing, acknowledge both sides of the argument rather than simply stating a preference. Use specific examples of global films you have studied to illustrate how cultural bridging works in practice. Remember that audience reception is active, not passive: different viewers from different backgrounds will read the same film differently. Link audience factors directly to the films studied in Component 2, explaining how cultural context shapes your response as a UK viewer.
